title: WV AI Watch: on the desk
description: Dated, sourced updates on West Virginia's data center and AI power projects.

items.title: PSC docket, MARL case: from Nov 18 to Nov 20 the docket adds six briefs, two protest letters, and a petition to protest with 27 signatures.

items.title: The United Mine Workers of America and West Virginians for Energy Freedom criticize the PSC's Fort Martin approval, saying it could threaten coal jobs and leave existing customers paying for data center demand. FirstEnergy has said the gas plant is meant as an addition to the coal plant, not a replacement.
items.content_text: The United Mine Workers of America and West Virginians for Energy Freedom criticize the PSC's Fort Martin approval, saying it could threaten coal jobs and leave existing customers paying for data center demand. FirstEnergy has said the gas plant is meant as an addition to the coal plant, not a replacement. Source: https://www.wvnews.com/news/wvnews/coal-miners-warn-of-job-losses-after-west-virginia-approves-fort-martin-gas-plant/article_adff36ab-c268-4edc-9c21-ec766f3f4910.html

items.title: Wheeling City Council hears the first reading of an ordinance regulating data centers in industrial districts, with standards for power demand and water use. WTRF reports a vote is set for the Dec. 1 meeting.

items.title: The PSC approves Mon Power and Potomac Edison's 1,200 MW gas plant at Fort Martin ($2.48 billion) and three solar projects ($182 million), with a customer surcharge the companies estimate starts at about $1.18 a month for residential customers.
items.content_text: The PSC approves Mon Power and Potomac Edison's 1,200 MW gas plant at Fort Martin ($2.48 billion) and three solar projects ($182 million), with a customer surcharge the companies estimate starts at about $1.18 a month for residential customers. Source: https://www.wdtv.com/2026/11/17/west-virginia-psc-approves-natural-gas-plant-mon-county-three-solar-projects/

items.title: Gov. Morrisey announces a $24 billion Appalachian Power investment: $17 billion in new natural gas generation (3.3 GW, three projects, to be completed in 2031) and $7.5 billion to keep its coal plants running until 2050. Locations are not yet announced.
items.content_text: Gov. Morrisey announces a $24 billion Appalachian Power investment: $17 billion in new natural gas generation (3.3 GW, three projects, to be completed in 2031) and $7.5 billion to keep its coal plants running until 2050. Locations are not yet announced. Source: https://westvirginiawatch.com/2026/11/12/gov-morrisey-announces-multi-billion-dollar-investment-in-west-virginia-power-plants/
